messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: High-severity: GPU OOMs detected during prefill on cluster-prod-us-west-2. Service: runtime-prefill. Multiple container restarts; 25% of requests returning 5xx. Paging oncall: @jen.
jen (oncall): I’m up. Thanks for the ping. Can someone drop the first failure log?
ryan: Pasting sample from node gpu-42: `cudaErrorIllegalInstruction` followed by oom and container SIGKILL. Stack shows prefill sequence length ~1.2M tokens for a single request (user reported very long document).
anya: Seeing same across 3 hosts in the same AZ. Memory climbed steadily during prefill and never trimmed; eviction happened once cache grew >80%.
mike: Rolling up impact: about 12% of production traffic to models with prefill enabled hit retries, some went to fallback model which is slower. Customers A and C reported increased latency and 5xx.
jen (oncall): Ok. Immediate mitigation options? Suggest disabling long-prefill-path for <some> model variants, or force trim on prefill to cap tokens, or temporarily route to coldmodel. Any cheaper/safer first step?
sarah: We can flip `prefill_disable_long_context` flag via config service in 30s — will prevent >256k token prefill but keep normal flows.
ryan: Also suggest `kv_cache_trim` aggressive for prefill requests. Patch is small: `runtime.flags.kv_trim_threshold=0.6` — should free KV cache actively during prefill.
jen (oncall): Do we have a one-click rollback? I can apply the config and monitor. Who's on standby to rollback if this causes regressions?
anya: I’ll watch nodes and container restarts, + tail `/var/log/runtime/prefill.log`.
infra-bot: Monitor set: node-restarts >=3 in 5m trigger pager. CPU/GPU mem dashboards linked: https://grafana/r/xyz.
jen (oncall): Applying `prefill_disable_long_context` now (runbook step 4). Command: `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/v1/flags -d '{"flag":"prefill_disable_long_context","value":true,"scope":"prod"}'`
jen (oncall): Done. Propagating. Waiting 60s for routing to take effect.
mike: Noted immediate drop in new prefill requests to the long-path. Still seeing some in-flight that will finish or OOM.
ryan: Pushed `kv_trim_threshold=0.6` to canary runtime group. Patch applied to 4/6 nodes in the group.
sarah: Customer updates: Lee from CS - can you confirm A and C have been notified?
lee (cust-success): Yep, emailed both with interim mitigation steps and ETA: monitoring for 30m then update. Both acknowledged.
anya: CPU/GPU mem graphs: seeing 40% reduction in steady-state mem growth in the affected pool; container restarts dropped from 1/m to 0.2/m.
jen (oncall): Good. Are there any nodes still flapping?
ryan: node gpu-42 still crashed once during in-flight heavy prefill, but it's stable now and has been drained for rebuild.
jen (oncall): Opened a P0 ticket to trace root cause: long prompt not trimmed + KV cache retention + kernel alignment issue on certain CUDA driver builds. Assigning to infra (ryan) and runtime (anya).
infra-bot: Attached basic diagnostics: `nvidia-smi dmon` snippet, container logs section.
anya: Quick root cause hypothesis: some model variants allocate pinned memory for prefill in a different codepath and on driver 525.x leads to fragmentation. For now, plan: 1) Keep `prefill_disable_long_context` on, 2) Backport `kv_trim` change to all runtime nodes, 3) Rebuild affected node images with driver 530.x, 4) Add runtime metric for 'prefill_token_count' so we can alert earlier.
mike: Customer impact summary for ops: ~5 customers affected with visible latency/5xx; no data exfiltration; most calls retried and serviced by fallback model but with degraded latency.
jen (oncall): Can infra proceed with node rebuilds? ETA?
ryan: Starting rolling rebuild of the 3 flagged hosts now — doing one at a time. Each rebuild ~12m.
jen (oncall): Thanks. Keep monitoring. If restarts go to zero for 30m and customer error rate back to baseline, we can close pager.
anya: Will add an automatic alert for `prefill_token_count > 500k` that triggers a separate warning channel before OOM.
lee (cust-success): I'll follow up with customers after 30m with an update and postmortem offer if they want.
jen (oncall): 20m in: error rate back to baseline (~1.1x normal), restarts negligible. Keeping the flag enabled for now.
mike: Noting CICD task: add validation to reject prefill >1M tokens at the API layer — created ticket DEP-7832.
jen (oncall): Reassigning P0 to postmortem owners: runtime (anya), infra (ryan), devex (sarah) for deploy guardrails.
jen (oncall): Closing pager for live mitigation. Keeping incident ticket open for RCA actions and customer follow-ups. Thanks team — great triage. :tada:
